source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 271: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 271): treat the initialization hang as an unproven symptom and do not infer a platform-specific cause. Use an authorized disposable allocation, a finite watchdog, redacted logs, and automatic cleanup of child processes and temporary state. Record backend, launcher, library/driver versions, scheduler/container, world size and placement, fabric, selected interface, topology, and the exact stage where progress stops; label each item measured, estimated, or unknown. Do not alter production settings until a reversible canary is justified.

Baseline and membership checks: assign a run ID and capture for every rank its host, global/local rank, PID, expected and observed membership, device mapping, GPU/NIC identifiers, software/configuration hashes, rendezvous/store parameters with secrets redacted, process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress time, backend debug output, interface/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall state, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, container device/shared-memory visibility, ulimits, and clock synchronization. Verify one process per expected rank, identical world size and rendezvous parameters, consistent collective ordering, reachable peers, and no hidden rank or duplicate.

Falsifiable hypothesis: one rank is not completing rendezvous or is selecting an unusable interface, so peers wait in collective initialization. This predicts rank-specific missing rendezvous or collective-entry evidence, or a failed path/interface check, and predicts that changing only the authorized interface/path choice or correcting the demonstrated membership mismatch makes a minimal all-reduce complete without changing application code. Falsify it if all ranks enter with matching parameters and the same reachable path, or if the failure persists under a controlled known-good interface and reduced world.

Controlled experiment: first run a minimal fixed-size all-reduce with a finite timeout, per-rank completion markers, and a checksum/correctness check. Run repeated matched trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements while holding software, tensor size, launch order, and timeout constant; change one factor per comparison. Test interface selection only in an isolated canary and collect per-rank outcomes. Report units and separate denominators for rendezvous success, collective correctness/checksum, latency distribution, timeout/hang, rank failure, transport error, and cleanup. Compare competing explanations including collective-order mismatch, wrong GPU visibility, topology/peer-access issue, network policy/MTU/firewall, resource exhaustion, container limits, and software incompatibility.

Decision and rollback: preserve the failing baseline, stop timed-out jobs, and roll back any diagnostic configuration when correctness, isolation, or bounded completion is not demonstrated. Escalate only with redacted artifacts and exact reproduction steps. The evidence plan narrows causes but does not claim a confirmed root cause; domain-expert review remains required.

Timeout or interface/topology changes can mask rather than fix the fault.
Diagnostics may expose sensitive endpoints or identifiers and require redaction.

Scope and assumptions (variant 280): treat the initialization hang as an unproven symptom and do not infer a platform-specific cause. Use an authorized disposable allocation, a finite watchdog, redacted logs, and automatic cleanup of child processes and temporary state. Record backend, launcher, library/driver versions, scheduler/container, world size and placement, fabric, selected interface, topology, and the exact stage where progress stops; label each item measured, estimated, or unknown. Do not alter production settings until a reversible canary is justified.

Baseline and membership checks: assign a run ID and capture for every rank its host, global/local rank, PID, expected and observed membership, device mapping, GPU/NIC identifiers, software/configuration hashes, rendezvous/store parameters with secrets redacted, process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress time, backend debug output, interface/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall state, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, container device/shared-memory visibility, ulimits, and clock synchronization. Verify one process per expected rank, identical world size and rendezvous parameters, consistent collective ordering, reachable peers, and no hidden rank or duplicate.

Falsifiable hypothesis: one rank is not completing rendezvous or is selecting an unusable interface, so peers wait in collective initialization. This predicts rank-specific missing rendezvous or collective-entry evidence, or a failed path/interface check, and predicts that changing only the authorized interface/path choice or correcting the demonstrated membership mismatch makes a minimal all-reduce complete without changing application code. Falsify it if all ranks enter with matching parameters and the same reachable path, or if the failure persists under a controlled known-good interface and reduced world.

Controlled experiment: first run a minimal fixed-size all-reduce with a finite timeout, per-rank completion markers, and a checksum/correctness check. Run repeated matched trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements while holding software, tensor size, launch order, and timeout constant; change one factor per comparison. Test interface selection only in an isolated canary and collect per-rank outcomes. Report units and separate denominators for rendezvous success, collective correctness/checksum, latency distribution, timeout/hang, rank failure, transport error, and cleanup. Compare competing explanations including collective-order mismatch, wrong GPU visibility, topology/peer-access issue, network policy/MTU/firewall, resource exhaustion, container limits, and software incompatibility.

Decision and rollback: preserve the failing baseline, stop timed-out jobs, and roll back any diagnostic configuration when correctness, isolation, or bounded completion is not demonstrated. Escalate only with redacted artifacts and exact reproduction steps. The evidence plan narrows causes but does not claim a confirmed root cause; domain-expert review remains required.
risks: Root cause remains unproven without per-rank artifacts and domain review.
Timeout or interface/topology changes can mask rather than fix the fault.
Diagnostics may expose sensitive endpoints or identifiers and require redaction.
